summary: Shenpen Hookham works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Michael M. Broido, as well as under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.
Shenpen Nangwa was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Patrul Rinpoche around 1885–1887. He held a post at Dzogchen Monastery from around 1900 to 1927.

Sherab Gyatso worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying at Labrang and Drepung Monasteries among others. He founded the Buddhist Association of China, serving as president (~1953–1966), and was dean of the Buddhist Academy of China in 1956.
Sherry Chayat works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Vassar College (~1961–1965) and trained under traditional teacher Eido Tai Shimano (~1967–1998), whom she succeeded in 2011.

Shichang Ma was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He served as a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in Peking University's Archaeology Department beginning in 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1925 to 1928 and later held a post there from around 1949 to 1968.

Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as an assistant at Kyoto University (~1959–1965) and as an associate professor at International Buddhist University (~1967–1974) and Shuchiin University (~1974–1985).

Shigeki Moro is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai Universities under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura. He served as associate professor at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and professor at Waseda University (2025).
Shigemasa Fukui is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from around 1954 to 1959 and later served as a professor there from around 1983 to 2005.

Shigemitsu Dando studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (~1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983), and Keio University (~1985–1987).

Shigeo Kamata was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, University of Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin University, and ICPBS.

Shigeru Gorai was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He held posts at Koyasan University, Otani University, Ryukoku University, and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore.
Shigeru Kato was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1903 to 1906 and later held a post there from around 1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957) and Harvard University (~1961–1967). He held posts at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1971–1994) and Tenri University (~1994–2004).

Shih Hu was a philosopher and scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cornell and Columbia under John Dewey, served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948), and was leader of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).
Shih-Hsiang Chen was a Sinologist who studied at Peking University from around 1932 to 1936. He later held a post at the University of California, Berkeley, from around 1945 to 1971.

Shili Xiong was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the China Institute of Inner Learning under Jian Ouyang in 1920. He held posts at Boone University, Zhejiang University, and as a lecturer at Peking University (1923–1955).
Shimin Geng was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China from around 1949 to 1953 and held a post there from around 1953 to 2000.

Shin Fujinaga is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 1992) and as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 2000).

Shin'ichi Chigusa is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Tohoku University (~1970–1978), where he later served as an assistant (~1980–1983), before holding a post at Yamagata University (~1983–2015).
